stem: A finance workload runs 24 hours a day at high, steady utilization, and a separate reporting job runs for two minutes once a night with no container image the team wants to build for it. Which TWO compute choices correctly match a workload to its need? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: EC2 On-Demand pricing charged hourly for the steady, high-utilization 24-hour workload
AWS Lambda running the steady, high-utilization 24-hour workload
EC2 with Reserved Instance pricing for the steady, high-utilization 24-hour workload
AWS Fargate running the two-minute nightly job
AWS Lambda running the two-minute nightly job

rationale: EC2 with Reserved Instance pricing suits utilization high and constant enough that a reserved commitment beats per-invocation serverless pricing, matching the steady 24-hour workload. Lambda fits a short, per-invocation job like the two-minute nightly report and needs no container image, matching the stated preference. On-Demand pricing charged hourly for the same steady workload costs more than a Reserved commitment for constant utilization, so it does not fit as well as the Reserved option for that workload. Lambda has a hard maximum execution timeout of 900 seconds per invocation and is billed per invocation, which does not fit a workload that must run continuously for 24 hours. Fargate requires building and managing a container image, which is exactly what the team said it did not want for the short nightly job.
